project_structure: Monorepo with packages: api (FastAPI + SQLAlchemy + Neo4j), web (React), shared (TypeScript types), db (migrations/seed). API uses async/await with pytest-asyncio for testing. Test infrastructure is minimal - only 2 test files exist (test_health.py, conftest.py). The API has 4 main route modules: herb.py, graph.py (Neo4j kg queries), verification.py (review module), chat.py (qa module).

relevant_files.rationale: Defines test_db and client fixtures using aiosqlite in-memory DB. All new tests should follow this fixture pattern.
Example async test with pytest-asyncio @pytest.mark.asyncio. Pattern to replicate for other API tests.
Contains pytest config: asyncio_mode='auto', testpaths=['tests']. Also defines dev dependencies: pytest>=8.3.0, pytest-asyncio>=0.25.0, httpx>=0.28.0
Neo4j graph service - core of kg module. All graph operations use async Neo4j driver. Tests need to mock or use test Neo4j instance.
QA module - answer_question() method with reasoning chain generation. Returns structured response with answer, sources, graph_data.
Review module - create_verification, get_verification, list_verifications, verify_verification endpoints.
Graph API routes: get_herb_graph, search_nodes, get_node, get_pending, find_path. Tests should cover these endpoints.
QA API routes: ask_question (POST /chat/question), get_session, create_session.
HerbModel SQLAlchemy model. Used in test_db fixture Base.metadata.create_all.
HerbCreate, HerbRead, HerbUpdate Pydantic schemas with strict mode.
Graph Pydantic schemas - Node types (HerbNode, ComponentNode, etc.) and Edge types.
Database connection setup. Tests override with in-memory SQLite via conftest fixture.

patterns: Testing framework: pytest + pytest-asyncio with auto asyncio mode. Test database: SQLite in-memory with aiosqlite driver via StaticPool. Test client: httpx.AsyncClient with ASGITransport. Test pattern: @pytest.mark.asyncio async def test_NAME(client, test_db): pattern. The conftest.py test_db fixture creates a fresh in-memory DB for each test using Base.metadata.create_all/drop_all. All services depend on AsyncSession from SQLAlchemy. Neo4j operations require mocking or a test Neo4j instance since the driver connects to real Neo4j.
dependencies: pytest>=8.3.0, pytest-asyncio>=0.25.0, httpx>=0.28.0 (for AsyncClient test client). aiosqlite for in-memory SQLite test DB. neo4j>=5.28.0 (async driver) - but tests need mocking. langchain>=0.3.0 (for chat service LLM integration).
integration_points: API routes depend on services: graph_service (Neo4j), chat_service (uses graph_service), verification routes (use both db and graph_service). Tests must mock graph_service for unit tests or use test Neo4j. Chat service answer_question() is the main entry point for QA testing. Graph API routes are /graph/herb/{name}, /graph/search, /graph/node/{node_id}, /graph/pending. Verification API routes are /verifications/ (POST/GET), /verifications/{id}, /verifications/{id}/verify. Chat API routes are /chat/question (POST), /chat/session/{id} (GET), /chat/session (POST).
constraints: 1) Neo4j driver connects to real Neo4j instance - tests need neo4j fixture or mocking. 2) Chat service uses langchain - LLM calls need mocking for unit tests. 3) All db operations must use AsyncSession with async/await. 4) In-memory SQLite test DB requires aiosqlite and StaticPool. 5) Tests should not share state between async functions - each test gets fresh DB via fixture. 6) The kg module (graph_service) uses singleton pattern with global graph_service instance.

clarification_needs.question: Should Neo4j tests use a test Neo4j instance (via docker) or mock the Neo4j driver?
clarification_needs.context: The graph_service connects to real Neo4j. Current test infrastructure has no Neo4j test setup.
options: Mock Neo4j driver for unit tests (faster, no external dependency)
Use test Neo4j container via docker compose (more realistic but slower)
Hybrid: mock for unit tests, integration tests use real Neo4j

options: Mock LLM responses for unit tests
Only test the non-LLM parts (entity extraction, graph queries, reasoning chain)
